Test identity and method continuity; mark revisions, breaks and missing periods.
State comparator, distribution, alternative explanations and the claim the measure can support.

contested_interpretations.interpretation: A larger count or capacity value indicates a better outcome.
contested_interpretations.counterevidence: Counts may reflect population, reporting or nameplate; service, quality, distribution and cost require separate measures.

contested_interpretations.interpretation: Official annual figures are automatically comparable over time.
contested_interpretations.counterevidence: Amtrak and manufacturing records expose changed cohorts, revisions and discontinued series that require explicit breaks.

decisive_evidence: Published measure dictionaries with numerator, denominator, inclusion and revision rules.
At least two compatible observations for trend language and more for stable longitudinal interpretation.
Outcome-specific comparators and distributional measures that preserve alternative explanations.
claim_boundaries: A count is not a rate, and capacity is not utilization.
Two dates do not create a valid trend when definitions changed.
Observed change is not automatically caused by the intervention under review.

foundation_chapters.title: Uncertainty, counterevidence and correction
foundation_chapters.deck: A living evidence system improves by recording contradictions, missing artifacts, revisions and bounded reversals rather than treating them as editorial failures.
executive_synthesis: Counterevidence in FTFN is concrete. A Waymo service authority sits beside a later flooded-roadway recall. Gateway's stable capacity panel sits beside a thermal-event and partial-return record. Federal monitoring obligations sit beside data that still needs manual correction. Amtrak's PIDS records expose incompatible completion inventories rather than hiding the mismatch.

These records do not require a binary verdict. They narrow the claim, identify an alternative explanation, expose a series break or set the next evidence test. Corrections should preserve the prior public state, date the revision and explain the effect on downstream pages. Silence or unavailable evidence remains unknown, not evidence of absence.
foundation_chapters.historical_baseline: The repository expanded from editorial notes into formal no-change receipts, blocker states, reconciliation records, alternative-explanation tests and retained correction history. The foundation explains how those controls shape public interpretation without changing any existing decision.
foundation_chapters.current_evidence_state: Published records contain many explicit limitations and some strong counterevidence pairings. Cross-record challenge coverage is still uneven, so the absence of a listed counterargument should not be read as consensus or confirmation.

conversion_chain.reading: Name what is unknown, why it matters and whether it reflects missingness, ambiguity or variance.
Attach a record that tests the same identity, mechanism, period or proposed explanation.
Record whether the original claim stands, narrows, is superseded or is withdrawn and why.
Update dependent pages and exports while retaining prior version, date and receipt.

contested_interpretations.interpretation: A negative event invalidates the whole technology or program.
contested_interpretations.counterevidence: Recalls, incidents and constraints are bounded by asset, operating domain and period unless broader evidence supports generalization.

contested_interpretations.interpretation: No located evidence means the event or artifact does not exist.
contested_interpretations.counterevidence: The operating method requires a bounded blocker or no-material-change state and prohibits inference from failed discovery.

decisive_evidence: A same-identity later record that directly tests the disputed claim or alternative explanation.
A dated adjudication stating the effect on claim scope and downstream artifacts.
A retained correction trail that lets readers reconstruct both old and current states.
claim_boundaries: Counterevidence is not automatically disproof.
Missing or inaccessible evidence is not evidence of nonexistence.
Correction changes the current reading without erasing accountable history.

foundation_chapters.title: Comparability, time and series breaks
foundation_chapters.deck: Comparison begins only after entities, measures, methods and periods are compatible—and stops when a material definition changes.
executive_synthesis: Several Published records exist primarily to prevent false comparison. The Annual Survey of Manufactures ends after 2021 and creates an explicit break. Amtrak's portfolio denominator and PIDS inventories change across reports. EPA sustains an annual water-reuse implementation record without a national operating-volume denominator. Battery records preserve asset identity and distinct market contexts.

FTFN therefore compares evidence structures before it compares results. A valid comparison states why the entities belong in a cohort, which measure is shared, how periods align and which revisions were applied. If any of those conditions fail, the appropriate product is a juxtaposition or gap—not a league table, trend line or score.
foundation_chapters.historical_baseline: The corpus progressed from individual dated signals to panels and series, then added explicit alternative tests, compatibility controls and series-break registries. Those layers document why some apparently similar records remain outside comparison.
foundation_chapters.current_evidence_state: The repository supports bounded within-entity and same-program comparisons in selected cases. Broad cross-jurisdiction and cross-asset outcome comparison remains limited because methods, periods and service definitions often differ.

conversion_chain.reading: Define why entities are comparable and which material differences remain.
Align unit, numerator, denominator, inclusion rule and source method.
Match operating periods, revisions, seasonality and exposure; declare lag assumptions.
Admit, qualify or reject comparison and publish the reason without ranking by default.

contested_interpretations.interpretation: Official records with the same label can be placed on one trend line.
contested_interpretations.counterevidence: Discontinued surveys, revised cohorts and incompatible inventories show that labels can conceal method changes.

contested_interpretations.interpretation: A common unit such as megawatts makes assets comparable.
contested_interpretations.counterevidence: Duration, market role, availability, incident state and service definition materially change the interpretation of nameplate power.

decisive_evidence: Versioned definitions and revision notes for every included observation.
A compatibility decision that names entity, measure, method, period and remaining differences.
A series-break marker and pre/post treatment whenever a material definition or cohort changes.
claim_boundaries: Juxtaposition is not comparison, and comparison is not ranking.
A common label or unit does not establish compatible meaning.
A series break cannot be repaired by silently carrying the prior denominator forward.
